claims.text: An integrated machine-learning framework for optimizing thermomechanical processing can enable stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations can concurrently enhance strength and ductility in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Refractory high-entropy alloys commonly face a strength–ductility trade-off.
The strength–ductility trade-off in conventionally processed refractory high-entropy alloys results from suboptimal microstructural control.
Machine-learning optimization of rolling reduction, annealing time and temperature, and aging conditions can produce tailored SCCPs.
The relevant strength and ductility improvements can occur at ambient temperature.
SCCPs comprise coherent lamellar and nanoparticulate precipitate structures formed in a stepwise manner.
A machine-learning framework can correlate processing parameters with the development of coherent precipitate microstructures.
Nanoparticulate precipitates pin dislocations and thereby contribute to strengthening.
Coherent lamellar interfaces permit dislocation transmission and shearing across precipitates.
Dislocation transmission and localized precipitate shearing relieve stress concentrations and help avoid premature crack initiation, preserving ductility.
Machine-learning-optimized processing will provide simultaneous strength and ductility improvements relative to conventional non-optimized processing.
Conventional strengthening routes typically improve strength at the expense of ductility.
The proposed approach is effective only in alloy systems capable of forming coherent nanoprecipitates and whose processing parameters can be reliably predicted by the machine-learning model.
The quantitative improvements and direct transferability of the machine-learning framework across alloy systems remain unvalidated.
